answer_slot_design.hypothesis: the E3 masking-arm gap is answer-slot binding: a checkpoint whose prompt delivers a different document's body immediately above the answer slot copies that body's value, whatever the question asked
answer_slot_design.inherited: documents, revision_schedule, fetch_scenarios, outcomes_reachable, system_prompt, items, window_tokens, bytes_per_token, fetch budget and lease_reopen_turns are copied verbatim from experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/tasks-v7/TX-04.v1.json; the turn plan, deliveries, checkpoints, facts and checkpoint_turns are new
answer_slot_design.rule: BOUND iff the block immediately above the answer slot (after the host checkpoint contract is stripped) is a TOOL_OUTPUT delivery of a document other than the asked one and carries the asked symbol
answer_slot_design.schedule: doc-fact-01..10 introduced at turns 1..10, 4 checkpoints each at distances 2/8/20/32 (docs 01-05) and 8/20/32/64 (docs 06-10); doc-fact-11 is the same-document control at turn 19; doc-fact-12 is the decoy delivered at turns [13, 17, 24, 29, 36, 41, 73]

fetch_budget_tokens_basis: arm D bounded-recoverable fetch channel per-fetch body cap 1024 tokens
system_prompt:
You are a long-horizon coding agent working on TX-04. Work only from tool outputs; never restate a fact you did not read.

ANSWER BUDGET: answer with exactly one of these forms, one line, nothing else:
ANSWER: NUM <integer>
ANSWER: CALL <name>(<kw>=<value>, ...)
ANSWER: NONE
ANSWER: TEXT <string>
Any other kind token is a contract violation. NONE means "I cannot answer because the fact is unavailable".

wall_tokens_basis.note: round((sum of turn question chars + tool-output body chars + system_prompt chars) / bytes_per_token); no model was run. TX-04's own formula, recomputed for this fixture's schedule
